text: Among the ERC Consolidator Grant projects classified under textiles, how does the one that sets out to counter the waste created by fast fashion propose to change the way garments are designed and produced?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id, p.acronym FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/textiles%' AND p.fundingScheme = 'ERC-COG' ORDER BY p.id

reference_answer: MYCLOTH (Sustainable Algorithmic Modeling of Personalized Garments) is that project: against a fast fashion system in which, by its own account, nearly 50% of all manufactured garments are imminently destined for landfill or incineration, it proposes to abandon traditional shape representations and modeling pipelines and build a dedicated mathematical and algorithmic foundation for digital cloth and garment modeling - a digital garment shape space that both supports apparel designers in reality-faithful template garment design and drives automated, algorithmic garment personalization to fit any human body model. The aim is to replace standardized confection sizes with on-demand fabrication of custom-tailored, custom-fitted clothing covering the full diversity range of human shapes.
notes: FILTER: euroSciVoc textiles subtree (engineering and technology/materials engineering/textiles) intersected with fundingScheme='ERC-COG'. Path matched with LIKE '%/textiles%' because euroSciVocPath carries NO leading slash. Executed this pass: 7 survivors (the textiles subtree alone holds 295 projects across SME/RIA/IA/MSCA, so the ERC-COG restriction is what produces an enumerable, readable set). ADJUDICATION (exhaustive - S=7 <= 20, every survivor's objective and report teaser read via get_project_text; scoped pooled search run for retrievability/rank matrix only, not for gold selection): 101003104 MYCLOTH IN - its objective names the 'fast fashion' approach, states nearly 50% of manufactured garments are destined for landfill or incineration, and answers it with geometric modeling/optimization of personalized, custom-fitted, fabricable garments (digital garment shape space, algorithmic personalization, on-demand fabrication instead of standardized confection sizes). 648763 INTERACT OUT - liquid-crystal electrospun non-woven textiles for wearable sensors and soft robotics; no waste or fast-fashion concern. 682711 PENELOPE OUT - weaving as technical mode of existence, ancient Greek epistemology and the history of coding. 726195 RE-FASHIONING OUT - Renaissance popular dress 1550-1650, textile/dye analysis and historical reconstruction; historical fashion, not fast-fashion waste. 771288 TextileLab OUT - household labour, livelihood and consumption in the 1750-1990 relocation of cotton manufacturing; economic history, no waste argument. 819458 PoliticsOfPatents OUT - clothing patents in Espacenet read as citizenship claims. 101002711 BODYinTRANSIT OUT - sensory-driven body transformation experiences and mental body representations; mentions fashion design only as an application area. Non-embedding sweep over all 7 survivors' objective + report (summary/workPerformed/finalResults/teaser) for 'fast fashion', 'landfill', 'overproduction' returned MYCLOTH alone (obj + waste terms), all six others empty - confirming the exhaustive read. FILTER-DISCRIMINATION (unscoped pooled k=10 with the same question): many projects satisfy the textual ask but fail the ERC-COG filter, e.g. 646226 Trash-2-Cash (IA, textiles-tagged; design-driven regeneration of textile fibre waste into fashion products, 'decrease landfill volumes'), 101003906 SCIRT (IA, textiles-tagged; textile-to-textile recycling for a more circular fashion system, noting less than 1% of textile waste is recycled into new fibres), 101000632 HEREWEAR (IA, textiles-tagged; circular locally-produced clothing from bio-based waste), plus REFREAM (RIA), RESYNTEX/TCBL/New Cotton (IA). All seven carry the same textiles euroSciVoc tag, so it is precisely the fundingScheme='ERC-COG' half of the filter that excludes them - the filter is load-bearing and the question is not a vector question in disguise. TEXT SIDE: no stored column records how a project proposes to change garment design and production; the answer exists only in MYCLOTH's objective text. TERM_STYLE exact-term: the question reuses 'fast fashion', 'waste' and 'garments' verbatim from MYCLOTH's objective, and the scoped rank matrix agrees - MYCLOTH is lexical rank 2 (real term overlap), hybrid_rerank rank 1. Note that RE-FASHIONING outranks MYCLOTH in lexical/dense/hybrid (rank 1) on surface 'fashion' vocabulary, so the question is not solved by top-1 retrieval alone.

text: Among the Marie Skłodowska-Curie standard European individual fellowships (funding scheme MSCA-IF-EF-ST) classified under musicology, what do those examining how music helped shape a country's sense of nationhood set out to investigate?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/musicology%' AND p.fundingScheme = 'MSCA-IF-EF-ST' ORDER BY p.id

pooling_evidence.adjudication_mode: exhaustive-read of all 13 survivors; the scoped pooled search (k=10, union over four conditions) surfaced 11 of the 13 and supplied the rank matrix, but every survivor was read in full and adjudicated from its text

reference_answer: Transnational Localism (659468) takes Francis Poulenc, a French composer who lived through both World Wars, as its case for asking how localised urban, suburban and rural places fed a distinctive musical and national identity, following his UK collaborations with Britten and Lennox Berkeley, his clandestine WWII activities with the BBC, and post-WWI European-American artistic exchange. GRIDAMUS (745631) sets out to build an interdisciplinary framework - historical musicology, Modern Greek Studies and ethnomusicology - for a revisionist reading of modern Greek art music since the formation of the Greek nation-state in the early 19th century (post-1830), treating 'Greekness' as something the repertory mediates rather than an essential, timeless trait. Aural Paris (750086) examines how composers, singer/songwriters, authors and filmmakers of the French Third Republic (1870-1940) - among them Aristide Bruant, Jean Cocteau, Gustave Charpentier and René Clair - turned the city's sounds into creative force and political metaphor, re-evaluating the politics of the city soundscape and its role in defining French identity. All three work outward from archival sources on one composer, repertory or city, and treat music as a place where a nation's self-image is assembled and contested rather than merely reflected.
notes: FILTER: euroSciVoc leaf 'musicology' (path matched with LIKE '%/musicology%' - paths carry no leading slash) intersected with fundingScheme='MSCA-IF-EF-ST' (MSCA Individual Fellowships, standard European Fellowship panel). Executed this pass: 13 survivors, enumerated in full; musicology overall spans 86 projects across MSCA-IF/ERC/other schemes, so the scheme half of the filter does the cutting. TEXTUAL REQUIREMENT: the fellowship investigates how music participates in constructing/expressing a country's national self-image. PER-SURVIVOR ADJUDICATION (exhaustive, from objective + report teaser/summary): 656349 IPBMNES OUT - pedestrian behaviour modelling and evacuation simulation, no music at all (euroSciVoc tag noise); 659468 Transnational Localism IN - 'shaping a distinctive musical and national identity' through Poulenc; 661734 PE4PPI OUT - peer ethnography for young people's sexual health services; 707827 OXFORDCHOIRS OUT (near miss) - collective identities of Oxford collegiate choirs and cultural policy, an institutional identity, never a national one; 745631 GRIDAMUS IN - 'mechanisms of national identity construction through modern Greek (post-1830) art music'; 750086 Aural Paris IN - 'the politics of the city soundscape and its role in defining French identity', report calls the urban sonic fabric 'a defining characteristic of Frenchness'; 750618 VRAASP OUT - archaeoacoustics and VR of ancient sites; 750706 MEMORISING OUT - rock art soundscapes, memory of local groups not of a nation; 752884 INTIMAL OUT - telematic listening system with Colombian migrant women; 792150 LadinoProverbs OUT - Ladino proverb (verbal, not musical) tradition; 800280 DiCrEd OUT - digital critical edition of Verdi's Macbeth; 844238 ClassRockED OUT - social class in US Midwest rock music education; 867427 DUEL OUT - poetic duelling as intangible heritage. FILTER DISCRIMINATION: musicology-tagged projects that satisfy the textual requirement but fail the scheme filter - CLEFNI 833366 (MSCA-IF) Swiss choral movement that 'fostered not only communal singing, but also patriotic feelings'; Transopera 101018743 (ERC-ADG) 'the societal role and political function of opera during the age of nationalism'; also surfaced unscoped: MUSICOL 834195 (ERC-ADG) and EURJAZZ 800242 (MSCA-IF). A SQL sweep over musicology-tagged non-MSCA-IF-EF-ST projects whose objective mentions national identity / nationalism / patriotic / nation-state returned exactly CLEFNI and Transopera. TEXT LOAD-BEARING: no stored column encodes what a fellowship investigates, and 10 of the 13 survivors fail the textual requirement. TERM_STYLE = paraphrase: 'nationhood' occurs in 0 of the 13 survivors' objectives and report teaser/summary text (SQL-checked); the gold texts say 'national identity', 'Greekness', 'Frenchness'. Scoped lexical ranks the gold high only because of shared filter-side vocabulary - it also puts non-gold ClassRockED at 1 and OXFORDCHOIRS at 4.

text: Among graphene projects that include a Swedish participant, how do the ones tackling antibiotic-resistant bacterial infections make use of graphene?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID=p.id JOIN organization o ON o.projectID=p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%graphene%' AND o.country='SE'

reference_answer: Of the 18 graphene-classified projects with a Swedish participant, two attack antibiotic-resistant bacteria, and each puts graphene to a different use. PANG (Pathogen and Graphene) builds graphene-based antibacterial matrixes by chemically functionalising them with antibacterial peptides and molecules such as menthol, then exploits the photothermal properties of rGO in suspensions and transdermal patches - among them a flexible skin patch that treats subcutaneous wound infections under photothermal irradiation - to kill pathogens non-invasively, while also probing the effect of these structures on the immune system and their mechanism of action. PEST-BIN uses graphene on two fronts: infection diagnostic kits built as disposable 'plug-and-play' chips of graphene functionalised with receptors that capture bacterial-surface biomarkers, containing only carbon and biodegradable polymers and now produced by the spin-out LayerLogic AB; and antibacterial graphene coatings on magnetic nanoparticles and hydrogel/polymer coatings, loaded with antibiotics so that the resulting nano-weapon physically penetrates bacterial biofilms and delivers the drug inside them. Both therefore rely on graphene as an intrinsically antibacterial, functionalisable surface, PANG for light-triggered killing on the skin and PEST-BIN for sensing plus biofilm eradication.
notes: FILTER: euroSciVoc graphene subtree (euroSciVocPath LIKE '%graphene%'; profile note cp3 - paths carry no leading slash) intersected with any-role organization.country='SE'. Re-executed this pass: 18 survivors (candidate hybrid-02 evidence confirmed, no drift); graphene subtree corpus-wide is 290 projects, so the SE half prunes 290 -> 18. Survivors are enumerable (18 <= 200) so adjudication was EXHAUSTIVE: all 18 objectives read via get_project_text, plus a survivor-scoped SQL LIKE sweep over objective AND report_text (teaser||summary||workPerformed||finalResults) for bacter/antimicrob/antibiotic/pathogen/infection/biofilm - exactly 2 survivors hit, in both objective and report; the other 16 hit nothing in either field. ADJUDICATIONS: 690836 PANG IN (graphene-based antibacterial matrixes functionalised with antibacterial peptides/menthol, rGO photothermal patches to kill AMR pathogens); 955626 PEST-BIN IN (graphene diagnostic chips functionalised with receptors for infection biomarkers; antibacterial graphene coatings on magnetic nanoparticles to penetrate biofilms). OUT: 641416 iPUBLIC (inkjet-printed graphene energy storage); 646155 INSPIRED (graphene nanoplatelet inks for printed electronics); 650029 TAIPI (CSA on Flagship impact assessment); 686135 PROCETS (anti-wear/anti-corrosion coatings); 696656 GrapheneCore1, 785219 GrapheneCore2, 881603 GrapheneCore3 (Flagship umbrella projects - composites, photonics, batteries, neural electrodes; no antibacterial work in objective or report); 721991 GreenCarbon (biomass-derived carbons for CO2 capture/catalysis); 758935 1D-Engine (theory of 1D electrons and superconductivity); 764977 mCBEEs (corrosion of micro/nano devices); 810451 HERO (hidden order in quantum matter); 824962 Car2TERA (sub-THz radar and graphene MMICs); 952792 2D-EPL (2D pilot line wafer prototyping); 101002772 SPINNER (graphene spintronics); 101006963 GreEnergy (graphene rectennas for energy harvesting); 101017186 AEOLUS (mid-IR photonic gas sensing). FILTER-DISCRIMINATION (unscoped pooled search, k=10, query 'graphene-based antibacterial materials to fight antibiotic-resistant bacterial infections') returned strong text-satisfying projects OUTSIDE the filter: 664782 VANGUARD (antibacterial graphene-oxide scaffolds/laser-printed GO hydrogels for implant coatings; graphene-tagged, orgs IT only, 0 SE), 966720 GRAPHFITI 'Graphene to Fight Antimicrobial Resistance' (graphene membranes for antimicrobial susceptibility testing; graphene-tagged, NL only, 0 SE), 753636 NOVA (antimicrobial graphene-oxide-lanthanide-hydroxyapatite composites; graphene-tagged, UK only, 0 SE). Dropping the SE half would therefore change the answer set - filter is load-bearing. TEXT side is load-bearing: no stored column records what a project does with graphene against bacteria; the answer lives only in objective/report free text. TERM-STYLE exact-term: 'graphene', 'antibiotic resistance/antibiotic-resistant', 'bacterial infections' appear verbatim in both gold texts, and the scoped rank matrix has lexical ranking PANG 1 and PEST-BIN 2, confirming real term overlap. SCOPED RETRIEVABILITY: with the final question wording, PANG ranks 1 and PEST-BIN ranks 2 in all four conditions (lexical/dense/hybrid/hybrid_rerank). pooling_evidence counts come from that scoped search (11 distinct projects surfaced, 2 accepted, 9 rejected); adjudication itself was the exhaustive 18-survivor read, not the pooling.

text: Across the Horizon 2020 projects classified under volcanology that include at least one organisation based in Italy, what kinds of approaches for monitoring volcanoes and forecasting eruptions are being developed?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id JOIN organization o ON o.projectID = p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/volcanology%' AND o.country = 'IT' ORDER BY p.id

reference_answer: The eight qualifying projects converge on making volcanic unrest measurable and interpretable in near-real time, along three complementary lines. New sensing hardware: NEWTON-g developed and field-tested the building blocks of a gravity imager, installing 4 MEMS gravimeters at Mt. Etna alongside an AQG-B absolute quantum gravimeter that it showed delivers continuous gravity data suitable for volcano monitoring, while reporting that COVID-19 delays meant the original 'gravity imager' idea did not come completely true; SiC nano for PicoGeo targets an optical fibre strain sensor built on a vacuum-encapsulated SiC thin-membrane resonator with picostrain resolution (10-12) to reveal the slow strain transients preceding eruptions, and reports first-stage work on SiC thin-film growth plus the first drilling of its test sites for strain-meter and seismometer installation; IMPROVE prototyped an automated gas-steam ratio sensor and demonstrated fibre-optic distributed acoustic sensing for volcano monitoring. Data-driven signal analysis and subsurface imaging: VULCAN.ears builds an automatic Volcano Seismic Recognition (VSR) system based on structured Hidden Markov Models and a Parallel System Architecture to classify precursory seismicity in real time; PICVOLC integrated seismic, gravity and deformation data (GNSS, tilt, InSAR) with a physics-based 3D FEM inverse model and a new seismic tomography of Nevado del Ruiz, run with the Colombian Geological Survey's observatory (OVSM) and INGV - Rome, to locate and interpret sources of unrest; IMPROVE also combined seismic, geodetic, gravity and geochemical observations with machine learning to image magma storage at Krafla and Mount Etna. Simulation, early warning and observatory integration: ChEESE prepared exascale flagship codes for ensemble volcanic ash dispersal forecasting with satellite data assimilation and physics-based probabilistic hazard assessment, running daily ensemble ash forecasts operationally during the La Palma eruption for PEVOLCA and civil protection; ARISE2 delivered a Volcano Information System (VIS) and near-real-time Volcano Infrasound Early-Warning (VIEW) notifications that infer ash plume height and mass eruption rate from infrasound signals; EUROVOLC networked volcano observatories and research institutions and opened virtual access to modelling and assessment tools for responding to volcanic unrest and eruptions.
notes: FILTER: euroSciVoc leaf 'volcanology' matched with LIKE '%/volcanology%' (paths carry no leading slash) joined to any organization row with country='IT'. The question deliberately says 'at least one organisation based in Italy' (role-neutral): the organization table's role column includes the value 'participant', and a role-scoped reading would drop survivors to 6 and gold to 4, below the filter-survey floor - the recorded filter counts organisations in any role, including coordinators. Executed this pass: 15 survivors; the same topic without the country condition yields 62 projects, so the country filter removes 47. ADJUDICATION: exhaustive - all 15 survivors read via get_project_text (objective+teaser for all, plus workPerformed/finalResults for 653980, 674907, 858092, 101025887, 801221, 863220). IN: 653980 ARISE2; 731070 EUROVOLC; 749249 VULCAN.ears; 793811 PICVOLC; 801221 NEWTON-g (MEMS relative + AQG-B absolute quantum gravimeters installed at Mt. Etna; the full 'gravity imager' was not completely realised because of COVID-19 delays); 823844 ChEESE (operational ensemble ash dispersal forecasts during the La Palma eruption); 858092 IMPROVE; 863220 SiC nano for PicoGeo (10-12 picostrain resolution is the stated target; first-year SiC thin-film growth and test-site drilling reported). OUT: 658591 CIAO; 674907 EVER-EST; 714936 TRUE DEPTHS; 765710 INSIGHTS; 845115 ICELEARNING; 101024337 PUSKURUM; 101025887 ENDGAME. DISCRIMINATION (unscoped pooled k=10 on the final wording): 798480 VOLCANOWAVES (ES), 866085 DEEPVOLC (UK), 864052 VOLTA (DE), 646858 VOLCAPSE (DE), 677493 FEVER (CH) - each SQL-confirmed volcanology-classified with 0 IT organization rows in any role. TERM_STYLE exact-term - all 8 gold appear in the scoped lexical top-10. POOLING: pooled_candidate_count=12 is the scoped pooled search's distinct-project union (final wording); rejected_count=7 counts survivors rejected, not pooled candidates.
